notes: robots.txt has 'User-agent: *' / 'Allow: /' with no Claude-specific disallow, so proceeded normally (verified fresh this pass). Accessed via Chrome tab only. The Home & Living mega-menu on /shop/home-living does NOT surface a visible 'Furniture' tile with children (its own embedded nav JSON shows /furniture as a leaf link with children:[]), but the dedicated department page https://www.myntra.com/furniture is a real, populated furniture department (13662 items) with its own facet-based sub-category tree - this is the furniture branch the prior Home-Decor pass deliberately excluded (its notes list 'Furniture' among excluded whole nav branches). Tree/qty source: the page's own embedded state window.__myx.searchData.results.filters.primaryFilters (id='Categories', 35 values) - this is the exact same data rendered in the visible on-page 'CATEGORIES' filter sidebar (cross-checked verbatim, e.g. sidebar text 'Sofa(854)' matches facet value Sofa=854). Sanity check: summing all 35 category facet values = 13661, versus page total 13662 (off by exactly 1 untagged product) - confirms these are exact, non-rounded, non-inflated backend counts, not a marketing widget. A 'Sub Categories' facet also exists but collapses to a single value 'Furniture' covering the whole 13662/13661 set (not a real taxonomy level), so the 35-value 'Categories' facet is the deepest usable level; Furniture is therefore emitted as one grouping row with the 35 categories as direct leaf children (no intermediate room-level grouping exists on this site). For every included/excluded borderline category, opened the filtered listing (https://www.myntra.com/furniture?f=Categories:<value>) and read product titles directly (Rule: node identity confirmed by matching h1/breadcrumb 'Furniture' and the on-page facet-panel count equalling the URL's item count in each case sampled: Inflatable Sofa and Bed=854, Home Temple=224, Hammock Swing=345, Notice Board=101, Step Ladder=40, Magazine Holder=9, Bird House=5, Umbrella Stand=2, Luggage Rack=1, Coat Stand=1, Shoe Rack=718, Drawers=115, Cabinet=104 - all matched the sidebar facet number exactly). EXCLUDED categories and why: Mattress (6506, bedding not furniture per project rule); Notice Board (101, wooden wall-mounted pin/bulletin boards, not furniture); Step Ladder (40, functional foldable stepping ladders/tools, not furniture); Magazine Holder (9, small standalone holder/organiser, not furniture); Bird House (5, garden/outdoor decor item, not furniture); Umbrella Stand (2, small entryway holder object, decor-adjacent accessory rather than structural furniture). INCLUDED with a flag: Drawers (115) is a genuine mixed rollup - sampled titles show real wood chest-of-drawers furniture (Ikiriya, THE ATTIC 'Wood Free Standing Drawers') interleaved with small standalone plastic storage-drawer organisers (Oddpod 'Premium Drawer', PSA/TEX-RO 'Organizer/Modular Drawer', DIWAM HANDICRAFTS 'Storage Drawers Box') with no site-side filter to isolate the furniture-only subset, so qty is set to null + flagged per project rule for unsplittable mixed rollups rather than guessed. Judgment calls kept IN scope (site files them under its own Furniture department and product tiles support the classification): Sofa Cum Bed / 'Inflatable Sofa and Bed' (dominated by foldable sofa-cum-bed furniture, a few inflatable air-bed items mixed in but not dominant); Home Temple (wooden pooja-mandir/temple cabinet units - a recognised freestanding wood furniture category in Indian retail); Hammock Swing (hanging/standing swing chairs - seating furniture, common 'jhula' furniture category); Shoe Rack (freestanding multi-tier shoe storage stands/cabinets, kept as furniture per the project's freestanding-shelving-unit and shoe-cabinet precedent, and because the site itself files the whole node under Furniture); Luggage Rack and Coat Stand (single-item categories but genuine hallway/bedroom furniture pieces per project scope). No mattress/bedding, lighting, mirror, rug/textile, or standalone storage-box categories were included anywhere in this department.
